correctness.rationale: Partition opposite vertices into n pairs; adjacent occupied pair signs alternate except seam signs must agree. For odd n all pairs occupy, forcing exactly two antipodal parity classes of cardinality n and no single swap. For even n the signed-cycle frustration demands at least one vacancy; one vacant pair yields exactly two sign-propagated n-1-vertex choices and all 2n translates I_r. Any single swap must move the vacancy to an adjacent pair, with unique insertion sign, yielding I_r~I_{r±(n−1)}. Since gcd(n−1,2n)=1 for even n, the exchange graph is C_{2n}; for odd n it is 2K1. Our independent exhaustive labeled-graph checker recovered optimum sizes/counts and exchange edges for n=3,...,8. The sign-cycle proof, not finite testing, covers every n≥3.
residual_risks: Checker covers n≤8 only; all-n step uses mathematical sign/frustration proof.
